headline: Rewindable proofs give weak verifiers a new route to check robust computations
summary: A new paper introduces rewindable interactive proofs, in which a verifier can restore an AI prover to an earlier saved state and continue the interaction from there. For robust oracle computations, the authors prove a relativizing protocol with a succinct verifier and a linear-time honest prover, without assuming that a prover is truthful or relying on cryptography. The paper reports a proof-of-concept MNIST-derived experiment and a BLAKE3 comparison, but the authors say the experiments are not a realistic scalable-oversight benchmark. The measurements use selected hardwired circuits; general preprocessing and real model-state restore costs remain unresolved, so deployed oversight benefits are not established.
